overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's account of one's own body. You'll be asked about one's own body, the body schema, the body schema vs. body image distinction, spatiality of situation, and motor intentionality.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty say one's own body is "permanent" in a way ordinary objects aren't?

options.html: Because the body lasts longer than most objects we use
options.text: Because the body lasts longer than most objects we use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Permanence isn't about duration. It's the body's constant presence as the point of view I can't leave or survey from all sides.

options.html: Because it's the point of view I can never leave
options.text: Because it's the point of view I can never leave
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! I can walk around a table, but not around my own body. It's what I perceive from, not one more thing I perceive.

options.html: Because its physical structure doesn't change over time
options.text: Because its physical structure doesn't change over time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The body changes. Its permanence is its constant presence as my point of view.

options.html: Because I always have a clear image of it in mind
options.text: Because I always have a clear image of it in mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Permanence isn't an image. It's the body's constant presence as the point of view from which I perceive.

forms.stemHtml: Leaning on a desk, you feel the pressure in your palms while the rest of your body trails behind. Which kind of spatiality does this illustrate?

options.html: Spatiality of position, since your body is at a location
options.text: Spatiality of position, since your body is at a location
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Spatiality of position is the coordinate space of objects. The leaning body is organized by its task.

options.html: Spatiality of situation, organized by the task
options.text: Spatiality of situation, organized by the task
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The body gathers around the task, anchored in the desk, rather than being located by coordinates.

options.html: Spatiality of perception, organized by vision
options.text: Spatiality of perception, organized by vision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That isn't one of Merleau-Ponty's categories. The leaning body shows spatiality of situation.

options.html: Spatiality of memory, organized by past postures
options.text: Spatiality of memory, organized by past postures
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That isn't one of Merleau-Ponty's categories. The leaning body shows spatiality of situation.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe the body schema, in Merleau-Ponty's sense? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A dynamic sense of the body's possibilities
options.text: A dynamic sense of the body's possibilities
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The body schema is the body poised for action.

options.html: A unified grasp of the body as a whole
options.text: A unified grasp of the body as a whole
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each part is given through its role in the whole.
Correct! The body schema is the body as oriented toward what it's doing.

options.html: An inventory of parts and their locations
options.text: An inventory of parts and their locations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty denies that the body schema is an inventory.

options.html: A picture of the body consulted by the mind
options.text: A picture of the body consulted by the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty denies that the body schema is an image.

forms.stemHtml: What is the term for the body's directedness toward things and goals through movement itself, aimed at things rather than coordinates, and not mediated by explicit representations? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Motor intentionality directs the reach at the cup, not at a computed location.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty calls this motor intentionality.

forms.stemHtml: In Gallagher's distinction, which of the following is an example of the body image rather than the body schema?

options.html: Keeping your balance while reaching for a high shelf
options.text: Keeping your balance while reaching for a high shelf
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Keeping balance is governed by the body schema, which works without awareness.

options.html: Walking through a doorway without judging its width
options.text: Walking through a doorway without judging its width
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is the body schema at work, governing movement without awareness.

options.html: Feeling self-conscious about your height in a photo
options.text: Feeling self-conscious about your height in a photo
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The body image is a system of perceptions, attitudes, and beliefs about one's own body.

options.html: Catching a falling cup before noticing it fall
options.text: Catching a falling cup before noticing it fall
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is the body schema at work, governing movement without awareness.

title: Body Schema and Motor Intentionality
